newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Colombia rebels ask Venezuela president to mediate.
newsitem.headline: Colombia rebels ask Venezuela president to mediate.

text.p: Marxist Colombian guerrillas have approached Venezuela's President Rafael Caldera to seek his support for talks to free 60 troops held prisoner since last August.
In a letter sent to Caldera by the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) and obtained by Reuters, the FARC said the Venezuelan president would be well-placed to end the six-month standoff.
"We think it decisive the contribution which the government you preside (over) could make to the Colombian people and the families of the military prisoners," said the letter, dated Jan. 22, 1997.
The 60 troops were captured during an attack on a military base in Colombia's southern jungle region Aug. 30. Another 27 soldiers were killed in the attack.
In the letter, the FARC told Caldera the troops would be freed if Colombia's President Ernesto Samper ordered the amry's withdrawal from certain areas in the south of the country.
President Rafael Caldera has made no public response to the FARC's invitation to mediate.
